findings: The exposed native mesh shows both bevel wheels, the transverse shaft, integral input pinion, clutch rings and twelve formed rivets per wheel. The support bushes and thrust stack remain separate linked parts.

The central cutaway exposes the four-dog clutch, gear webs, separate inner bushes and the bearing races/balls. The wider section connects this drive to the existing planetary train without changing stored placements.

The thrust-bearing section shows the printed envelope and distinct race/cage/ball boundaries. Sixteen balls per bearing and their internal geometry are inferred; appearance does not establish historical bearing construction.

The source panels preserve local-bevel and inherited-output registrations at one unchanged scale. The32.112857mm axial disagreement remains plainly visible. Sleeve and bush proportions change to fit printed bearing dimensions and retained sun/drum datums.

The local overlay shows differing wheel tooth-band/web contours and a narrower modeled pinion cone than the illustration. Printed tooth count/pitch constrain the model; the source drawing, source scale and inferred tooth/profile dimensions have not been forced into agreement.

The provisional input shaft extends beyond the illustrated end. The enlarged canvas exposes this discrepancy; its axial shoulders and total length must be revisited with the absent bearing/housing/coupling stack.

Rivet head and clutch-ring profiles differ from the source. The alternating twelve-hole pattern, quarter-inch ring flange, engagement clearances and cast seating profiles remain documented hypotheses.
not_qualified: Historical pressure angle, tooth corrections and manufactured contact pattern
Historical bearing internals and shaft/profile dimensions
Full motion, load capacity or complete assembly sequence
